title: Context-fanning latency notes
content:
Purpose:
Quick lab notes for the 'context fanning' hypothesis: long contexts that partially overlap across concurrent requests can be amortized by reusing KV-cache segments and avoiding duplicate attention work. Small exploratory runs to find sweet spots and failure modes.

Setup summary:
- Model: open-gptx-13B (prod-like quantized bobtail profile)
- Hardware: single A100-40GB (dev pool), local docker instance of runtime v0.9.1+patch
- Workload: synthetic arrivals (zipf alpha=1.2) mixing prefixes of 128, 512, 2048 tokens; 70% of requests share a prefix cluster of size 4 (context-fan group)
- QPS: ramped 10 -> 250 (steady-state window used at 150 qps)
- Measuring: tail latencies (p50/p95/p99), kv-cache hit rate, tokens/sec, CPU -> host, GPU utilization, memcp transfers

Raw snapshots (steady at 150 qps):
- run A (baseline, no re-fan optimization): p50=36ms, p95=212ms, p99=542ms; kv-hit=13%; tokens/s=22k; GPU util=68%
- run B (fanned-prefix coalescing enabled, aggressive reuse): p50=34ms, p95=180ms, p99=320ms; kv-hit=47%; tokens/s=28k; GPU util=73%
- run C (fanned reuse + conservative batching): p50=38ms, p95=160ms, p99=290ms; kv-hit=49%; tokens/s=26k; GPU util=70%

ASCII latency distribution sketch (run B, steady):
[0-50ms]  ########### (p50=34ms)
[51-200ms] ####### (p95~180ms)
[201-400ms] ### (p99~320ms)
[400ms+]  #

Observations / quick hypotheses:
- Context-fanning boosts kv-hit dramatically (13% -> ~50%) which directly reduced work per request.
- p99 improvement large but sensitive to burst alignment: when many fans finish simultaneously we see transient p99 spikes (resource contention at KV read path + memcpy).
- Conservative batching smoothed out p99 further but slightly decreased tokens/s. tradeoff: throughput vs tail.
- GPU memory copies (host<->device) appear to be the hot stall during big fan reunions — need to inspect RDMA/GPUDirect path on dev fleet.

Failure modes noticed:
- Fan group size > 8: coalescing logic starts increasing latency because cache eviction churn grows (eviction thrash). threshold around 6-7 seems critical.
- Cold restart: first 30s of sustained load shows elevated p99s as caches warm; current warmup heuristics under-allocate priming requests.
- Heterogeneous seq-len mixes: very long tails (2048) block GPU for longer and reduce benefits of fanning on short requests.

Short todo list:
- [ ] Add telemetry spans on KV read pipeline to measure memcpy vs compute time (obs: Devon)
- [ ] Try pinned buffers + GPUDirect in a controlled run (Mira to coordinate infra/QE)
- [ ] Add adaptive fan-size cap (default 4, max 6) and run staircase load to measure p99 knee
- [ ] Draft a short perf note for eng-rt channel with graphs and thresholds (target: decision for canary)

Experiment notes (parameters to sweep next):
- fan_group_size: 1..8 step 1
- batch_timeout_ms: 8, 12, 20, 32
- kv_cache_eviction_policy: LRU vs CLOCK vs cost-aware TTL
- priming_rate: 0%, 2%, 5%, 10% of traffic as 'prime' requests

Links / references remembered:
- Slack thread: #serving-runtime "context-fan-proto" (last ping Jan 20)
- JIRA: JIRA-3221 (fan coalescing prototype)
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/pr/1123 (fanning basic impl)
- Confluence: CONFLUENCE-7892 (notes + diagrams)

Open questions:
- Can we avoid host<->device memcpy penalty by reordering fanned payloads to prefer already-resident buffers?
- Is eviction thrash due to global LRU being too coarse for mixed-length workloads?
- What's the right guardrail for fan-group size in multi-tenant (noisy neighbor) environments?

Closing quick conclusions:
- Context-fanning shows promising drop in p99 with moderate fan sizes (4-6) and helps throughput.
- Must address memcpy contention and eviction thrash before rolling to canary.
- Next runs: pinned buffers + adaptive fan cap + priming 5% for 15m window.

Notes to self: keep this log rough; results will go into a short internal note if next sweep confirms.
